STARLINK’S MESH NETWORK IS ESSENTIALLY UNBREAKABLE

Here’s why Starlink’s architecture is so resilient:

•  Thousands of satellites work together as a massive, self-healing mesh in low-Earth orbit.
•  If one satellite fails or is taken out, traffic instantly reroutes through dozens of others — no single point of failure.
•  Inter-satellite laser links and multiple ground gateways create redundant paths, so even major disruptions (cable cuts, natural disasters, or targeted attacks) can’t easily knock it offline.
•  Elon Musk has described it as nearly impossible to kill: “You really can’t kill it… it will keep on running because they’re all just simply nodes working together as a whole.”
This is why Starlink has become the go-to lifeline in war zones, disaster areas, and remote regions where traditional internet fails completely.
When cables are cut or towers go down, Starlink keeps working.
The network isn’t just reliable — it’s designed to survive scenarios that would break any ground-based system.
That resilience is one of the biggest reasons Starlink is changing global connectivity forever.

STARSHIP IS ONE OF THE GREATEST ENGINEERING FEATS IN HUMAN HISTORY

Elon Musk on Starship’s true purpose:
“Starship is designed to make life multiplanetary, otherwise extreme overkill for mere Earth sector activity.”

Starship isn’t just a big rocket.
 It’s the first fully reusable, orbital-class spacecraft designed from the ground up to make humanity multiplanetary.

Its importance is hard to overstate:
•Full reusability — Both the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage are meant to fly again and again, slashing launch costs from hundreds of millions to just a few million dollars per flight.
•Orbital refueling — The ability to transfer hundreds of tons of cryogenic propellant between ships in orbit unlocks the Moon and Mars with massive payloads. No other vehicle can do this at scale.
•Massive payload capacity — 100–150+ tons reusable to orbit (future versions even higher). Enough to deliver entire habitats, power systems, and crew in single flights.
•Rapid cadence — Only Starship can launch often enough to deliver the millions of tons needed to build a self-sustaining city on Mars.

This is the rocket that turns the dream of becoming a spacefaring civilization into engineering reality. 

Every flight, every catch, every refueling test is a step toward securing humanity’s long-term future.

Elon Musk is an outstanding leader.  

Ten years ago he had a crazy idea: let’s train a computer vision model that can drive a car.  

It was an idea that was ahead of its time. We didn’t have the giant compute clusters we have now. An end-to-end neural network handling the entire driving task felt like a pipe dream.  

His team faced massive technical challenges. Pushback. Jeers and screams from journalists who said it would never work. Resistance from regulators.  

And he persisted. He kept investing. Any other CEO would have killed the project. He didn’t. He never gives up.  

Now he’s cracked it — rolling out the first pure-vision self-driving cars in history. Europe just got FSD for the first time, starting in the Netherlands, with more countries coming fast.  

Huge credit to Ashok, the Tesla AI team, Andrej Karpathy, the chip team, and every technical genius who made it real. But it took true visionary leadership to assemble that team and let them thrive for a decade.  

You can disagree with him, mock him, glorify or vilify him… but you can’t ignore him. Because he changes things. He pushes the bar higher. He leads our species forward.  

Thank you to the entire Tesla team (including Elon) for building products that make our lives better every single day — especially the self-driving. As Tesla Owners in Silicon Valley, we feel the impact more than most.  

This is just the beginning for Europe. The future is here. 🚀🇳🇱

🚨 Major Legal Victory for Tesla & Elon Musk! 🏆
Today, Vice Chancellor Bonnie W. David of the Delaware Court of Chancery dismissed multiple consolidated shareholder derivative lawsuits against Elon Musk and the Tesla board.
The cases — involving allegations around insider trading, the Twitter/X acquisition, and AI resource allocation — were tossed not on the merits, but because Tesla shareholders voted in 2024 to reincorporate in Texas and adopt a forum-selection bylaw requiring all derivative litigation to be filed exclusively in Texas courts.
Key excerpt from the ruling:

“I will not second-guess Tesla stockholders’ chosen forum by purporting to weigh the advantages and disadvantages of Texas law and procedure relative to our own… The owners of the corporation voted to require that derivative litigation be filed in a Texas forum. On the present facts, it is not inequitable to enforce their decision.”

This is a clear win for shareholder sovereignty. Tesla owners spoke, and the court honored their decision instead of allowing forum-shopping in Delaware.
Any refiled cases will now head to Texas business courts, which apply a more deferential business judgment rule — far friendlier to boards and executives.
Tesla’s move to Texas continues to pay dividends. Governance respected. Momentum building. 🚀
